s1.syndrome_frame: A cardiac abnormality with a systolic murmur and abnormal ECG findings in a young pregnant woman
salient_findings: Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
key_facts: 29-year-old primigravida woman
No history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
Vital parameters within normal limits
Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Normal sinus rhythm with heart rate of 70 beats/min on ECG
Complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
Fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads on ECG
No significant ST-T segment changes on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
Large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography
Normal cardiac output on right-sided heart catheterization
Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium
Pulmonary vascular resistance: 1.8 Wood units

shortlist.label: Atrial Septal Defect
shortlist.why_kept: Large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Ventricular Septal Defect
shortlist.why_kept: Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region and abnormal ECG findings

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Septal Defect
shortlist.why_kept: Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Patent Foramen Ovale
shortlist.why_kept: Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium

shortlist.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
shortlist.why_kept: Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography and abnormal ECG findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography and a step-up in oxygenation from the superior vena cava to the right atrium supports the diagnosis of Atrial Septal Defect.

rejected.label: Ventricular Septal Defect
rejected.why: The echocardiography findings of a dilated right atrium and right ventricle with a large defect are more consistent with an atrial septal defect than a ventricular septal defect.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Septal Defect
rejected.why: The ECG findings and echocardiography results do not indicate the presence of an atrioventricular septal defect, which typically involves abnormalities of the atrioventricular valves.

rejected.label: Patent Foramen Ovale
rejected.why: A patent foramen ovale would not typically cause the significant left-to-right shunt and dilatation of the right atrium and ventricle seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
rejected.why: Ebstein's anomaly involves abnormalities of the tricuspid valve and right ventricle, which are not indicated by the provided ECG and echocardiography findings.
